hooks: "Upper halls" — the high seat of the old kings, as against a lower Sala downstream.
Gamla Uppsala's royal burial mounds are from the 500s, and the pagan temple beside them was described by a German chronicler in 1070.
Its university, 1477, is the oldest in Scandinavia, and Linnaeus taught here — his garden is still planted to his own plan.
"Western Aros" — aros is a river mouth, so the name is the western river mouth, against Uppsala’s eastern one.
ASEA, which became ABB, was founded here in 1883 and made the town an electrical engineering centre.
Its Anundshög is Sweden’s largest burial mound, with stone ship settings beside it.
"Log islet" — stock, a log, plus holme, an islet: the city began on a fortified island in 1252.
It is built on fourteen islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic, and its archipelago has about 30,000 more.
The Vasa, a warship that sank on her maiden voyage in 1628, was raised in 1961 and is 98% original timber.
"Fortress of the Geats" — Göta plus borg, founded in 1621 by Gustav II Adolf with Dutch engineers, which is why it has canals.
Volvo was founded here in 1927, and the name is Latin for "I roll".
Its Liseberg is the largest amusement park in Scandinavia, and the city holds Sweden’s biggest port.
Probably from malm, a sandy or gravelly ground, plus haug, a mound.
Danish until 1658, and now joined to Copenhagen by the Öresund bridge, which becomes a tunnel halfway across.
Its Turning Torso, twisting 90 degrees over 54 floors, was the tallest building in Scandinavia when finished.
